path_builder_foe.description: The path-and-block antagonist: a CatalystFoe that walks and BUILDS — dropping primitive blocks (pyramid/wedge/cube by curriculum stage) to wall the player's route. Befriend it with the catalyst and it stops building and clears the wall it made. Win by outrunning it to the exit, or by changing its mind.
path_builder_foe.name: Path Builder Foe
path_builder_foe.qfep_connection: The wall and the one who builds it are the same problem, solved the same way — you do not break the maze, you befriend its author.

path_game_controller.description: Win/lose controller for the path-and-block game. Wins on reaching the teleporter OR befriending every foe; loses on the watchdog's blocked-path timeout. Pops a pixel thumb over a befriended foe and a pixel heart on a win.
path_game_controller.name: Path Game Controller
path_game_controller.qfep_connection: A game is two truths and a verdict — can you still cross, and did you have to destroy anything to do it; the thumb answers the second.

path_cube.description: Path-and-block game brick: a solid cube wall. Has a collider and is NOT path_passable, so the path watchdog routes around it. The foe's blocking primitive.
path_cube.name: Path Cube (wall)
path_cube.qfep_connection: The watchdog routes around it not because it is heavy but because it never joined the path_passable group: blockedness is a membership status wearing a material costume. Beside the wedge it shares size, shader, and floor — the wall is the rule it carries, nothing else.

path_wedge.description: Path-and-block game brick: a walkable ramp. Tagged path_passable so the path watchdog routes THROUGH it — a cube the player can climb. The gate primitive.
path_wedge.name: Path Wedge (ramp)
path_wedge.qfep_connection: One diagonal face plus enrollment in path_passable turns the same footprint from sentence into gate: the pathfinder routes through, the body climbs. Passability is first declared in a group name and only then enacted in geometry — permission precedes the ramp.

path_pyramid.description: Path-and-block game brick: a 1m-base pyramid mound that BLOCKS the path (you can't cross a peak). Supports the grid wireframe shader. The first primitive in the foe's progression.
path_pyramid.name: Path Pyramid (mound)

path_watchdog.description: Runtime referee for the path-and-block game. BFS-checks every half-second whether a walkable route still exists from the player to the teleporter; draws it as a floor ribbon (green open / red blocked) and restarts the level if the path stays blocked past a grace window.
path_watchdog.name: Path Watchdog
path_watchdog.qfep_connection: A level is solvable until someone proves it isn't — reachability turned from a design-time guarantee into a live, clocked stake.

orb_test_rig.description: Test fixture for the orb gesture slice. Place in a map to bootstrap OrbGestureDetector (under XR rig) and CatalystOrb (under self), and optionally spawn three test creatures around itself. Two-handed forms a sustained dose; one-handed fires a burst with per-hand cooldown. Replaces the catalyst projectile mechanic.
orb_test_rig.name: Orb Gesture Test Rig
orb_test_rig.qfep_connection: Capability-as-relation. The orb is the relation between the palms while the gesture is held; it dissolves when palms part. No inventory item — see /blog/2026-05-11-cognitive-water and doc/ORB_GESTURE_SLICE.md.

pusher_block.description: A red cube that translates back and forth along one axis, physically pushing the player into pits. Uses AnimatableBody3D for proper physics collision. The translation transformation made dangerous.
pusher_block.name: Pusher Block
pusher_block.qfep_connection: Translation as force — the simplest transformation becomes the most direct threat. The block does to the player what the player does to objects.

sweeper_block.description: A blue beam that rotates around a central pivot, sweeping players off edges into pits. Don Quixote's windmill — the world spins and you must time your crossing. Uses AnimatableBody3D.
sweeper_block.name: Sweeper Block
sweeper_block.qfep_connection: Rotation as sweep — the transformation you feel in your inner ear. The windmill doesn't attack you; you attack it, and it wins because it is the world.

grower_block.description: A cube that pulses between tiny and huge, physically pushing the player as it grows. When small you can pass, when large it fills the corridor and squeezes you into the pit. Color shifts from green (safe) to red (danger).
grower_block.name: Grower Block
grower_block.qfep_connection: Scale as pressure — the uncanny transformation that changes everything while appearing to change nothing. You don't move; the world moves into you.

armadillo_droideka.description: Foldable machine-creature enemy with rigid scutes, split equator rings, deployable legs, and fire-bolt burst attacks.
armadillo_droideka.name: Armadillo Droideka
armadillo_droideka.qfep_connection: Locomotion and weapon are one fold: the scutes that make it a wheel hinge open into an armored biped, and the state machine only ever moves between two readings of the same shell. Nothing is added at deployment — the threat was already present in the ball, compressed.

armadillo_eggling.description: Small aggressive roll-form variant focused on contact pressure, tuned for swarm behavior.
armadillo_eggling.name: Armadillo Eggling
armadillo_eggling.qfep_connection: The base droideka with everything switched off except rolling and touch: zero shots, zero detection radius, contact damage 9. Threat reduced to proximity, and in groups the flanking looks coordinated though no line of code coordinates it.

becoming_catalyst.description: An evolving hand force that grows alongside the player. Not a weapon of destruction but a tool of transformation, becoming, and boundary dissolution. Each Lab sequence unlocks a new expressive mode — from slow cubes to calming fields to swarm intelligence.
becoming_catalyst.name: The Catalyst
becoming_catalyst.qfep_connection: Embodies the full QFEP trajectory: from order (primitives) through entropy (randomness) to the edge of chaos (fractals, L-systems) and collective emergence (swarms). The catalyst IS the curriculum made tangible.

catalyst_pedestal.description: A one-meter wireframe cube display case with the Becoming Catalyst crystal floating and rotating inside. Place this in lab spawn areas. The player walks up, sees the glowing crystal, and grabs it — the cage fades away as the crystal absorbs into their hand.
catalyst_pedestal.name: Catalyst Pedestal
catalyst_pedestal.qfep_connection: The cage frames the invitation. Not protection but presentation — the moment before transformation, when the tool exists waiting to be claimed.

wedge_skill_pickup.description: A floating orange prism that unlocks the wedge_placer mode on the catalyst bracelet when grabbed. DNA: housing selects how the skill is kept until it is yours (cage = the one-meter wireframe cube, plinth = a solid column offering it, open = no housing at all); after selects what the site does once it is taken (fade = dissolve and free, remain = a dimmed empty housing left standing). Use #housing:plinth#after:remain.

dna.default: housing=cage, after=fade - the cage branch calls the original _build_cage() unchanged and the fade branch still queue_free()s, so all 12 existing placements look and behave exactly as before
dna.was: zero exports and apply_grid_config() was a bare pass: one fixed wireframe cage, as though a cube around a power were a neutral container
dna.note: The cage was an unexamined argument — it says a capability is a specimen you must reach into. plinth says it is conferred, open says nobody thought to fence it. after=remain leaves a scar where the power was taken; it is a time-domain axis and invisible to a still capture.

wedge_skill_pickup.name: Wedge Skill Pickup
wedge_skill_pickup.qfep_connection: The wedge teaches that not everything fits in a box. Slopes, ramps, and angles expand the vocabulary of space.

blockbuilderentity.description: A creature that builds with blocks — constructing and deconstructing grid structures as it moves. The world-shaping hazard that treats the grid as raw material.
blockbuilderentity.name: Block Builder Entity
blockbuilderentity.qfep_connection: It eats the map by the vertex and pays the harvest back as a cage — a hive of blocks raised around the player out of the dissolved room, a thought-label narrating the ledger overhead. Hazard and level design collapse into one loop: the architecture is hostile because the architect is.

branching_vine.description: L-system vine growing from a root point. Turtle graphics interpretation builds cylinder branches that reach toward the player. Damage prunes random branches. Formal grammar becomes organic growth.
branching_vine.name: Branching Vine
branching_vine.qfep_connection: One rewrite rule — F becomes F[+F][-F]F — plus a bias term leaning each branch toward your position: it does not chase, it compiles toward you every three seconds. Pruning is the only counterargument the grammar understands.

bricoleur_golem.description: Asymmetric golem built from mismatched primitives. Rebuilds itself from random parts after damage — each reconstruction unique. Exhausts after 3 rebuilds. Teaches bricolage: creation from whatever is at hand.
bricoleur_golem.name: Bricoleur Golem
bricoleur_golem.qfep_connection: Damage is a commission: each hit scatters the six body slots and the rebuild draws new random primitives into them, never the same golem twice. The exhaustion counter admits what bricolage costs — three reinventions and the improvising body runs out of flux.

dna.default: rig=free + mark=none returns before allocating anything; 100 placements unchanged.
dna.note: APPEARANCE ONLY - collision, damage, timing and triggers are untouched, because existing maps depend on this artifact's hazard behaviour. RENAMED from `mount` to `rig` after the review: exhibit_furniture#mount:<lookup_name> already means the artifact seated ON that bed across 500+ placements, and this meant the rig holding the target - two opposite senses of one token is a trap for whoever writes the next map.

catalyst_target.description: A practice target that flashes, explodes, and respawns when struck. Its visible states change quickly, but the target remains recognizably the same object across idle, hit, destroyed, and restored phases. Movement options add patrol and orbit patterns without changing that core identity. It is a compact lesson in state transition.
catalyst_target.name: Catalyst Target
catalyst_target.qfep_connection: Transformation here is discrete state change: intact, flashing, destroyed, respawned. Identity persists while S moves through a small cycle of visibly distinct modes.
catalyst_target.capacity: TRACK a target through hit, destroy, and respawn states while keeping its identity legible.
interactions: hit the target with catalyst projectiles
switch between static, patrolling, and orbiting motion via config
change the target shape to compare different visual states
watch the respawn loop reset the object after destruction

chromatic_field.description: RGB zone hazard with three overlapping translucent spheres cycling through hue. Damage type depends on the dominant color channel — red heat, green poison, blue cold. Teaches color mixing and perception.
chromatic_field.name: Chromatic Field
chromatic_field.qfep_connection: Hue is repurposed as a damage taxonomy — whichever channel dominates the cycling phase decides whether you burn, poison, or freeze. Color stops being appearance and becomes protocol; reading the spectrum correctly is the only armor on offer.

collision_crasher.description: Central body with 5 tethered physics blocks that bounce and collide with elastic collision math. Impulse vectors visible as arrows on impact. Momentum conservation made tangible.
collision_crasher.name: Collision Crasher
collision_crasher.qfep_connection: F_force: momentum conservation made tangible — five tethered blocks colliding elastically around a central body, impulse arrows at every impact. What is exchanged is never lost, only redirected.

constraint_web.description: 5x5 grid of superposition tiles representing a constraint satisfaction problem. Tiles collapse on step; contradictions explode. Graph coloring as minefield — no two adjacent tiles may share a color.
constraint_web.name: Constraint Web
constraint_web.qfep_connection: Every tile flickers through the colors it might still be until your footfall collapses it, and the no-two-adjacent constraint propagates outward from where you stood. An emptied domain detonates — contradiction made a physical event, billed to whoever committed first.

data_tree_walker.description: Binary search tree of sphere nodes connected by cylinder edges. BST insert with values 1-7; visible tree rotations on damage. Walks on its leaf nodes. Data structures made physical.
data_tree_walker.name: Data Tree Walker
data_tree_walker.qfep_connection: Seven values in a balanced BST, and the abstraction is made to carry weight — it stands on its own leaf nodes. Damage triggers visible rotations: the structure defends its O(log n) the way a body defends its posture.

deltahedron_creature.description: A creature whose body IS its mesh net. Flat at fold_amount=0, assembled convex solid at fold_amount=1. All equilateral triangles — Cauchy's rigidity theorem guarantees structural integrity when closed. Species: tetrahedron (4), octahedron (8), icosahedron (20).
deltahedron_creature.name: Deltahedron Creature
deltahedron_creature.qfep_connection: Cauchy's rigidity theorem does the character design: closed, convex, all-triangle, the finished body cannot flex — so vulnerability lives entirely below fold_amount 1, in the unfolding. Species differ only in net topology; the genome is a crease pattern.

deltahedron_stages.description: Five octahedra in a row at fold_amount 0%, 25%, 50%, 75%, 100%. Shows the complete net-to-solid fold progression in one glance. Blue (flat) to gold (assembled).
deltahedron_stages.name: Deltahedron Stages
deltahedron_stages.qfep_connection: One fold variable sampled five times and laid in a row: the octahedron's whole becoming, flat net to rigid solid, spatialized so the eye can walk the derivative. Time traded for distance — a transformation rendered as still life.

edible_mushroom.description: Pickable mushroom with transformative effects. RAND Corporation 1955 meets fungal spores — historical randomness made edible. Consume to trigger perceptual shifts.
edible_mushroom.name: Edible Mushroom
edible_mushroom.qfep_connection: Eating is implemented as proximity — hold it within 0.25 m of the camera and consumption fires, the mouth inferred from the head. Swallowing, the one gesture VR cannot give you, is skipped straight to its consequence: a shader rewrites perception and the form that caused it dissolves.

escher_stairwalker.description: Minimalist figure walking an impossible staircase loop. Always appears to climb but stays at the same height. Invulnerable while on stairs; glitches out to lunge. Impossible geometry as armor.
escher_stairwalker.name: Escher Stairwalker
escher_stairwalker.qfep_connection: Every step is locally valid; the loop sums to zero height — and inside that contradiction it cannot be hurt. It becomes vulnerable only when it glitches off the stairs to lunge: touching shared space is the price of leaving the representation.

fallingblocks.description: Environmental hazard that spawns falling block formations. Gravity as threat — the grid raining down. Dodge, shelter, or ride the cascade.
fallingblocks.name: Falling Blocks
fallingblocks.qfep_connection: A timer hands one cube at a time to gravity, and a hit costs position rather than flesh — you are posted back to spawn. Danger reduced to a schedule: no aim, no chase, just physics keeping an appointment above your head.

fibonacci_snake.description: Triangle strip coiled in a golden spiral unfolds into a slithering sine-wave snake. Phi encodes rest, sin encodes motion. Same vertices, same faces — only positions change.
fibonacci_snake.name: Fibonacci Snake
fibonacci_snake.qfep_connection: Rest is a golden spiral, motion a phase-shifted sine, and fold_amount is the only word the body has for the difference. No vertex is added or removed between coil and slither — identity survives as topology while every position defects.

fibonacci_snake_stages.description: Five stages: Fibonacci spiral to sine snake. Golden ratio coil unfurling into wave locomotion. Same vertex and face count throughout.
fibonacci_snake_stages.name: Fibonacci Snake Stages
fibonacci_snake_stages.qfep_connection: Phi-spiral and sine snake share every vertex and every face; the five stages merely lerp coordinates between the two poses. Two apparent species collapse into one topology — morphology exposed as a slider position, not an essence.

five_leg_critter.description: Five-legged procedural walker. Odd symmetry forces asymmetric gait patterns — starfish-like radial locomotion.
five_leg_critter.name: Five Leg Critter
five_leg_critter.qfep_connection: Placed at 72°, no foot has a mirror partner, so the step rule cannot relax into any inherited gait — every stride is improvised against the stretch threshold, one leg at a time. Five is the prime that keeps locomotion honest: walking with no symmetry to lean on.

flora_landscape.description: Renders the Folding Zoo nature_layer.json as a 3D landscape. Vertex-colored ground mesh with MultiMesh flora on top.
flora_landscape.name: Flora Landscape
flora_landscape.qfep_connection: A JSON layer file stands up as terrain: ground types become vertex colors, flora entries become MultiMesh instances, the rng seed pinned at 12345. Landscape as a saved document — the same nature every load, which is exactly what a document promises and a landscape never does.

fold_demo_critter.description: Four-segment folding creature — wings spread open and tail lifts as fold_amount increases. Demonstrates BoneFoldSolver with spring dynamics, energy gating, and misfold. The simplest possible folding body.
fold_demo_critter.name: Fold Demo Critter
fold_demo_critter.qfep_connection: Four segments, one spring solver, and a state machine that only spreads the wings when the world reads as safe — the tail lift waits behind wing progress. The gating is the point: unfolding as trust made mechanical.

fold_wall.description: Triangulated curtain pooled flat on the ground rises into a hanging drape. Columns cascade left to right with sine billow for fabric feel. Same vertices, same faces.
fold_wall.name: Fold Wall / Curtain
fold_wall.qfep_connection: A floor's worth of triangles hinges up into a curtain, columns cascading left to right with a sine billow laid over the rigid grid. The vertices that lay pooled now hang from the same faces — verticality as a remembered posture, not new geometry.

folding_zoo.description: Six-zone interactive showcase of the fold system — bone fold, chain fold, shell fold, state parade, misfold, and spring tension. All three solvers demonstrated with debug overlays.
folding_zoo.name: Folding Zoo
folding_zoo.qfep_connection: Six enclosures, three solvers, one sinusoidal _global_fold breathing through everything — comparative anatomy where specimens differ only in how they interpret the same scalar. That misfold gets its own zone matters: failure is admitted as a fold family, not an exception.

foliage_showcase.description: All 8 synthetic plant types side by side — grass, flower, fern, mushroom, reed, tree, bush, vine. Low-poly procedural meshes for MultiMesh instancing.
foliage_showcase.name: Foliage Showcase
foliage_showcase.qfep_connection: Eight plants in a police lineup, each a low-poly mesh built for MultiMesh multiplication — the botany here is logistics, nature pre-formatted for instancing. Before a forest can exist in this world, each species must first become a part number.

force_field.description: Dual-nature force zone: every hazard is also medicine. Fire warms or burns. Poison kills or reveals. Q-FEP: same potential, different restraint, different manifestation. Bring a mediator object into the field to transmute hazard into benefit.
force_field.name: Force Field
force_field.qfep_connection: Central demonstration of Q-FEP: identical potential under different relational constraint produces opposite outcomes. The player experiences this directly.

four_leg_critter.description: Four-legged procedural walker. Quadruped gait with diagonal pairing — walk, trot, gallop emerge from phase relationships between legs.
four_leg_critter.name: Four Leg Critter
four_leg_critter.qfep_connection: The feet sit at the four corners and none is told about the others: each simply steps when the body's drift stretches it past its threshold. Whatever reads as a trot is a settlement among four independent deadlines — the vertebrate gait recovered as emergence, not choreography.

fractal_hydra.description: Central body with branching heads on cylinder necks. Damage splits a head into two half-size copies — fractal branching up to depth 3. More heads means more attacks but less damage each. Cut one head, two grow back.
fractal_hydra.name: Fractal Hydra
fractal_hydra.qfep_connection: Punishment is its growth function: strike a head and two return at half scale, the pattern re-instancing itself down to depth three. Self-similarity as defense means your attacks are its recursion calls.

goomba_box.description: Folding cardboard box that patrols corridors. Stomp from above to flatten it — topology as vulnerability. Side contact deals damage.
goomba_box.name: Goomba Box
goomba_box.qfep_connection: Six faces, one weakness: the lid. The state machine grants it anger — DETECT, CHARGE — but its topology sealed its fate in advance; power sits unevenly on a body's surfaces, and the player learns to read bodies for their unguarded plane.

gradient_hunter.description: Sleek predator with orbiting sample-point particles. Gradient descent pathfinding toward player — gets stuck in local minima, anneals out with random teleport. Machine learning as locomotion strategy.
gradient_hunter.name: Gradient Hunter
gradient_hunter.qfep_connection: The loss function is you: six samples estimate the gradient of distance-to-player and it descends. Walls make local minima, so it does what optimizers do — waits three seconds, then teleports, and calls its desperation annealing.

grammar_markov.description: Tetrahedron with 4 colored state-faces. Markov chain transition matrix determines attack patterns — visible transition probabilities. Matrix mutates over time. Stochastic grammar made combative.
grammar_markov.name: Grammar Markov
grammar_markov.qfep_connection: Its behavior is legible exactly once: watch long enough and the transition matrix becomes learnable — then, every three cycles, the probabilities mutate. A stochastic grammar that punishes the statistics it invites you to gather.

graph_weaver.description: Network of 8 sphere-nodes connected by cylinder-edges. Reconfigures edges to create shortest path toward player with visible BFS/DFS traversal. Can cast edges as projectile attacks.
graph_weaver.name: Graph Weaver
graph_weaver.qfep_connection: Connectivity is the whole predator: it rewires its spanning tree into a shortest path aimed at you, walks a BFS wave along it, and can spend edges as projectiles. The attack surface is literally the adjacency list.

gridagent.description: Grid-traversing hazard agent spawned from map tokens like `gridagent:copy`.
gridagent.name: Grid Agent
gridagent.qfep_connection: A creature that walks the array — traversing the grid cell by cell, copying and patterning as it steps. The array given an inhabitant: where the other exhibits show the structure, this one shows what it is like to MOVE through indexed space, a body reading the lattice one address at a time.

hazards_demo.description: Test arena for all hazard creatures. Spawns plasma critters, stick tools, dormant egg-plant octapods, and an active crawler in a dark atmospheric arena with moody lighting and fog.
hazards_demo.name: Hazards Demo
hazards_demo.qfep_connection: The test arena where the danger fauna are let out together — plasma critters, crawlers, dormant egg-plants. Chance with consequences: the room where randomness stops being a visual and starts costing something.

helix_cylinder.description: Vertices on a helix form triangles into a closed faceted cylinder. Pineapple diamond topology. Flat triangle grid unfurls into a twisted tube. Kresling-inspired.
helix_cylinder.name: Helix Cylinder
helix_cylinder.qfep_connection: A flat triangle grid closes into a twisted faceted tube by lerping each vertex onto a helix; the pineapple's diamond lattice appears the moment the sheet's edges are identified. The cylinder was a quotient of the plane all along.

helix_cylinder_creature.description: Runtime fold creature — flat triangle grid folds into twisted faceted cylinder. Pineapple topology. Same vertices, same faces, only positions change. Driven by fold_amount.
helix_cylinder_creature.name: Helix Cylinder Creature
helix_cylinder_creature.qfep_connection: A cylinder is a flat grid that has agreed to identify its edges; here the agreement is continuous, fold_amount sliding the same triangles between page and tube. Aliveness is located in the twist — the shear that mere rolling-up would never add.

helix_fold.description: A triangle strip coils from flat zigzag ribbon into a helix via sin/cos. Five stages showing the fold progression. DNA springs spiral shells.
helix_fold.name: Helix Fold
helix_fold.qfep_connection: A zigzag ribbon coils into a spring with nothing but sin and cos per vertex, five stages standing side by side like specimens. The DNA iconography is earned honestly: a helix is what a strip does when both of its coordinates start rotating.

hull_crusher.description: Morphing convex polyhedron with orbiting point-nodes. Fires points as projectiles — each launch shrinks the convex hull. Points respawn over time. Teaches computational geometry through combat.
hull_crusher.name: Hull Crusher
hull_crusher.qfep_connection: Every attack is a vertex spent, and the hull — its body — shrinks to the extent of what remains. A geometry that pays for aggression out of its own definition, until respawn timers quietly restore the fiction of an inexhaustible form.

index_sentinel.description: A walking 4x4 grid that fires cells by [i][j] index, teaching array traversal through attack patterns. Row-major order, visual telegraphing of the next index.
index_sentinel.name: Index Sentinel
index_sentinel.qfep_connection: [i][j] with a muzzle: cells telegraph before firing in strict row-major order, so surviving means having internalized the traversal. Indexing stops being notation the first time it aims at you.

inflate_flock.description: Icosphere inflates from a point using vertex flocking — pressure pushes out, separation prevents overlap, cohesion holds shape. Organic breathing inflation. Same vertices, same faces.
inflate_flock.name: Inflate Flock
inflate_flock.qfep_connection: Inflation without a balloon equation: each vertex is a boid feeling outward pressure, separation from neighbors, cohesion toward the group, and the sphere emerges as their negotiated settlement. The surface breathes because no vertex is in charge.

isosurface_trap.description: Blobby metaball surface from point charges. Scalar field bulges toward player; contact equals damage proportional to field strength. The implicit surface made dangerous.
isosurface_trap.name: Isosurface Trap
isosurface_trap.qfep_connection: There is no wall, only a sum of charge-over-distance and a threshold: you are inside when the equation says so, and damage scales with the field's value at your body. The charges drift toward you — the boundary you are trying to read is also reading you.

joint_articulator.description: Central body with 6 limbs, each using a different joint type — hinge, ball, slider, revolute, prismatic, fixed. Each limb moves per its constraint. Joint physics made visible.
joint_articulator.name: Joint Articulator
joint_articulator.qfep_connection: Six limbs, six constraint vocabularies — hinge, ball, slider, revolute, prismatic, fixed — one body forced to speak them all at once. A taxonomy walking: each joint's freedom is exactly what the others are forbidden.

kaleidocycle_enemy.description: Tumbling ring of tetrahedra with 4 attack modes. Rolls toward player while continuously rotating through itself. Each face color triggers different attack: Fire (red), Ice (blue), Spike (purple), Shield (gold).
kaleidocycle_enemy.name: Kaleidocycle
kaleidocycle_enemy.qfep_connection: A closed kinematic chain where every attack face is always present, only rotated out of view: fire, ice, spike, and shield are one body's phases, not four weapons. When the shield face lands, invincibility arrives by pure topology of turn.

kresling_spire.description: Kresling origami sniper tower - twisting cylinder that extends from compact disc to tall tower. Rolls as disc to reposition, rises by untwisting to snipe from elevation, collapses rapidly to relocate.
kresling_spire.name: Kresling Spire
kresling_spire.qfep_connection: In the Kresling fold rotation and translation are one motion: to rise and snipe it must untwist, to flee it must twist flat. It also enforces a standoff, backing away as you close, so the fight happens at the tower's chosen range, not yours.

lifeform_walker.description: Walking creature with a 6x6 Game of Life grid on its torso. Living cells provide armor; Conway's rules run each tick. Dead automaton reinitializes. The cellular automaton made corporeal.
lifeform_walker.name: Lifeform Walker
lifeform_walker.qfep_connection: Its armor is not chosen, it is computed: Conway's rules tick across the torso and whichever cells happen to live are the plates that hold. Defense delegated to emergence — the creature hardens or opens depending on what a 6x6 automaton decides to become.

loving_triangle.description: A triangle-shaped companion that dances with the Becoming Catalyst. Triangles are the atom of all 3D worlds — every mesh reduces to triangles. This entity makes that visible. Not an enemy — a relational partner. It responds to each catalyst mode with its own transformation: folding, tiling, compressing, expanding. Evolves through tiers as lab sequences complete.
loving_triangle.name: Loving Triangle
loving_triangle.qfep_connection: The triangle embodies relational identity: the self constituted through encounter. Same potential (catalyst projectile), different relational context (triangle vs wall vs enemy), different manifestation. The simplest polygon that creates enclosure — the other that completes the becoming.

maze_spinner.description: Crystalline core that procedurally generates rotating maze walls. DFS-based maze generation with new random seed every 8 seconds. Navigate the gaps or take wall damage. The algorithm IS the enemy.
maze_spinner.name: Maze Spinner
maze_spinner.qfep_connection: DFS carves a perfect maze, then the seed rerolls every eight seconds and it carves another — memorization, the classic labor of maze-solving, is structurally worthless here. The corridor is rented, never owned, and it rotates while you rent it.

mesh_morpher.description: Shape-shifting creature morphing between sphere, cube, torus, and cylinder. Each topology has a different attack pattern — roll, slam, spin, sweep. Mesh topology as combat strategy.
mesh_morpher.name: Mesh Morpher
mesh_morpher.qfep_connection: Sphere rolls, cube slams, torus spins, cylinder sweeps — each attack is what that genus affords and nothing else. Identity-as-topology made hostile: to survive it you must read shape as constraint, not costume.

miura_crawler.description: Miura-ori folding enemy - flat corrugated sheet that crawls like an inchworm. Lies flat and nearly invisible, pops up when player approaches, uses zigzag locomotion. Can squeeze through gaps when flattened.
miura_crawler.name: Miura Crawler
miura_crawler.qfep_connection: One degree of freedom is a whole animal: cycling the fold amount corrugates a flat sheet into inchworm locomotion, and flatness doubles as camouflage. The threat is legible only when the geometry commits.

noise_field.description: 10x10 grid of height-varying tiles driven by Perlin noise. High tiles are danger zones, low tiles are safe. Noise scrolls continuously — the landscape of randomness shifts under your feet.
noise_field.name: Noise Field
noise_field.qfep_connection: Perlin's trick — randomness with spatial correlation — is what makes the danger legible at all: high red tiles announce themselves through their smooth neighborhoods. The field scrolls, so safety is a gradient you surf, not a place you reach.

octapod_crawler.description: Procedural 8-legged wall-crawling creature. Headcrab meets octopus. Patrols surfaces, detects player, chases and leaps. Can be stunned with fire. Future: befriend in lab, evolves through game.
octapod_crawler.name: Octapod Crawler
octapod_crawler.qfep_connection: It enters the world as a category error — pod, plant, egg, food? — and stays undecidable until the player's approach resolves it into enemy. Hostility here is not a property but a reaction: the crawler is dangerous because it was surprised.

octapod_ik.description: Eight-legged IK walker variant. Pure inverse kinematics locomotion without CharacterBody3D physics — legs find surfaces procedurally. The mathematical octapod.
octapod_ik.name: Octapod IK
octapod_ik.qfep_connection: Not a creature but the contract its whole family signs: eight skeleton chains, each FABRIK-bent toward a marker a SpringArm presses against the ground. The one-to-eight leg critters are subsets of this rig — a body plan kept as a reusable scene file, ancestry as infrastructure.

one_leg.description: Single IK leg demo — the fundamental unit of procedural locomotion. One joint chain finding ground contact. The building block from which all multi-legged creatures emerge.
one_leg.name: One Leg
one_leg.qfep_connection: The progression's axiom: one skeleton chain, one spring-found contact point, and a body that must bounce because balance on a single foot can only ever be serial. Everything the later critters elaborate — plant, stretch, step — is reduced here to whether the leg can reach the floor at all.

origami_bird.description: Origami crane that progresses through four fold stages: egg seed (0.0) → standing crane (0.4) → walking with alternating gait (0.6) → full wingspan flight (1.0). Twelve segments, paper-white materials, spring-damped fold dynamics. One fold_amount variable drives the entire lifecycle.
origami_bird.name: Origami Bird
origami_bird.qfep_connection: Twelve segments and a single scalar carry a crane from egg through standing and a sinusoidal walking gait to full wingspan — locomotion modes are just bands on the fold_amount axis. A lifecycle compressed to one dimension, with spring dynamics deciding how fast the paper is allowed to live.

origami_droideka.description: Magic-ball inspired fold shell using accordion pleats and braided ring bands; rolls compressed and deploys to fire.
origami_droideka.name: Origami Droideka
origami_droideka.qfep_connection: The same pleated shell is wheel, turret, and shield depending on where the fold sits; inflation_fire_bias decides how much firing exposes the core. Constraint doing the work of transformation — the sheet never changes, only its commitment.

origami_pyre_plane.description: A folded-paper rectangle of fire that sits beneath transport cubes. Its creased surface cycles through affine transformations — scale pulses, rotation sweeps, positional drift — while the rectangular shape remains invariant. Demonstrates that identity persists under transformation. Lethal on contact.
origami_pyre_plane.name: Pyre Plane
origami_pyre_plane.qfep_connection: It cycles scale, rotation, translation — exactly the transformations that preserve its rectangle — while the creases smolder orange; the invariant is the shape, the hazard is the heat. An affine-identity lesson taught by a floor that kills you for standing on the proof.

paradox_stalker.description: Two overlapping ghost silhouettes that swap which is real every 3 seconds. 50% chance damage passes through the wrong ghost. Zeno's paradox: sometimes halves distance to player instead of closing it.
paradox_stalker.name: Paradox Stalker
paradox_stalker.qfep_connection: Only one silhouette is real at a time and the bit flips every three seconds; strike the other and the blow passes through nothing. Sometimes it Zeno-steps, halving the distance instead of closing it — a hunter quoting the argument against motion while moving.

particle_emitter_hazard.description: Nozzle firing lifecycle-colored spheres with manual particle pool. Cycles between cone, fountain, and spiral emission patterns. Birth-white to active-yellow to dying-red. The particle system as weapon.
particle_emitter_hazard.name: Particle Emitter
particle_emitter_hazard.qfep_connection: Every projectile wears its age, birth-white cooling to dying-red, so dodging means reading lifecycle rather than trajectory. And the pool of thirty makes finitude the mechanic — even a weapon is a population with a birth rate.

pattern_mine.description: Mines with SDF contour rings marking danger zones. Cross the zero-contour and they detonate. Different ring shapes, pulsing indicators, and respawning after cooldown. Signed distance as survival instinct.
pattern_mine.name: Pattern Mine
pattern_mine.qfep_connection: The minefield publishes its own danger function: the torus rings at 0.3, 0.6, 0.9 are literal contour lines of the signed distance that detonates at zero. Rare honesty in a hazard — the mathematics of your death is fully disclosed, and still the boundary gets crossed.

plasma_critter.description: Shapeshifting energy substance — a critter that takes form based on relational context. Raw form shocks on contact. Touch with a stick → fire torch. Touch water → healing aura. Touch crystal → power orb. Q-FEP: same potential, different restraint.
plasma_critter.name: Plasma Critter
plasma_critter.qfep_connection: Raw it shocks, on a stick it becomes torch, in water it heals — the substance never changes, only the mediator, stored in code as a Form enum switched by whatever touches it. Harm and care as relational outcomes of one energy: the dual-nature claim run at creature scale.

proximity_spawner.description: Spawns enemies when player enters radius. Respawns after enemy death. Configure with type, spawn_radius, despawn_radius, respawn_delay.
proximity_spawner.name: Proximity Spawner
proximity_spawner.qfep_connection: E_entropy: the vent that answers approach — it spawns when the player comes near, so population is a function of attention. Nothing exists in the room until presence calls it out; the spawner makes observation itself a physical cause.

qfep_calibrator.description: Morphing dodecahedron with 3 parameter beams — phi (rotation speed), delta_e (damage), constraint (detection). Parameters oscillate, creating emergent behavior from their interaction. The QFEP laboratory's creature.
qfep_calibrator.name: QFEP Calibrator
qfep_calibrator.qfep_connection: Three sinusoids — phi, delta_e, constraint — never reference each other in the code, yet the creature's moods emerge from their beat frequencies. F_order stacked on F_order still yields E_flux: the coupling happens in the body, not in the equations.

recursion_spiral.description: Fibonacci spiral of shrinking sphere nodes spawned at golden-angle intervals. Each node is 0.618x parent size up to depth 5. Recursive cleanup on death. The golden ratio as creature architecture.
recursion_spiral.name: Recursion Spiral
recursion_spiral.qfep_connection: The same 137.5 degrees that packs sunflower seeds packs threat: each node spawns at the golden angle, 0.618 the size of its parent, damage thinning as 1/depth. Phyllotaxis without a plant — the optimum does not care whether it arranges seeds or ordnance.

resonance_chamber.description: Transparent box with standing wave bars at node positions. Damage at wave nodes, safe at anti-nodes; harmonic frequency shifts every 8 seconds. Sound physics as spatial puzzle.
resonance_chamber.name: Resonance Chamber
resonance_chamber.qfep_connection: The standing wave partitions the room into lethal nodes and safe anti-nodes, and every eight seconds a new harmonic redraws the partition. Safety here is not a place but a solution to cos(n·pi·x/L) — and n keeps changing.

scissor_stalker.description: Spider-like enemy with Hoberman scissor linkage legs. Legs extend 3x their compact length for dramatic reach. Stalks with partially extended legs, pounces by rapidly extending, slams down to attack.
scissor_stalker.name: Scissor Stalker
scissor_stalker.qfep_connection: Amplification as menace: one angular parameter runs through the Hoberman linkage and a small joint change becomes threefold reach. Even the walk is only phase-offset sines on the same bars — no animator, just geometry paid out.

shell_roller.description: Icosahedron creature that retracts into a kickable shell. Kick it to send it rolling — it bounces off walls and damages other enemies on contact.
shell_roller.name: Shell Roller
shell_roller.qfep_connection: Retracting for safety produces exactly the projectile form: the kick that protects the player weaponizes the creature against its own kin, and momentum conservation arrives with a body count. Defense and ammunition were the same shape all along.

six_leg_critter.description: Six-legged procedural walker. Insect-like alternating tripod gait — three legs always grounded. The most common arthropod configuration.
six_leg_critter.name: Six Leg Critter
six_leg_critter.qfep_connection: Six thresholds firing independently keep drifting toward the insect answer — three feet down, three swinging — because with legs at 60° that is simply what does not fall over. Four hundred million years of hexapod convergence restaged as the accident of a step rule.

spatial_voronoi.description: Ground plane divided into Voronoi cells by drifting seed points. Each cell has a different danger type — safe, damage, slow, heal. Seeds drift and types shuffle, remapping the partition. Spatial decomposition as territory.
spatial_voronoi.name: Spatial Voronoi
spatial_voronoi.qfep_connection: Territory is nothing but nearest-neighbor arithmetic: your cell is whichever drifting seed you are closest to, and its verdict — safe, damage, slow, heal — reshuffles on a six-second clock. Borders wander because centers do; the map is a consequence, never a commitment.

sphere_droideka.description: Armadillidiidae-style spherical droideka. Rolls as compact ball of overlapping shell plates, unfolds to tripod stance with shield dome and twin blasters. Star Wars droideka inspired.
sphere_droideka.name: Sphere Droideka
sphere_droideka.qfep_connection: The trade is written into the state machine: as a ball it is fast and unhittable, deployed it is armed, shielded, and rooted — mobility and firepower held as strict complements, never both at once. Minimum surface for maximum volume, then the geometry cashes its efficiency in as armor.

spring_hopper.description: Coil spring creature that bounces rhythmically. Land on top when compressed to get launched upward — Hooke's law as creature.
spring_hopper.name: Spring Hopper
spring_hopper.qfep_connection: F = -kx given eyes and a patrol route: compression is stored potential, and the player's trick is to arrive at maximum displacement, riding the hazard's own restoring force upward. Threat and elevator are one mechanism, distinguished only by timing.

spring_mass_bouncer.description: 3x3 grid of sphere mass-nodes connected by springs with Hooke's law physics. Deforms on contact; spring tension equals damage. Visible soft-body simulation as creature.
spring_mass_bouncer.name: Spring Mass Bouncer
spring_mass_bouncer.qfep_connection: Nine masses and F = -kx is the whole psychology: contact damage scales with the tension you provoke, so it hurts you exactly as much as you deform it. Softness here is not gentleness — it is stored energy waiting on a displacement.

stick_tool.description: A simple wooden stick the player can grab. Hold near a Plasma Critter to transform it into a torch. The mediator between player and plasma — the relational bridge.
stick_tool.name: Stick Tool
stick_tool.qfep_connection: By itself it does nothing — no damage, no state, just a tip that lets plasma change ontology from hazard to torch. Mediation is the whole mechanic: the grasped stick extends the arm, and the extended arm re-signs the treaty with fire.

swarm_hive.description: Stationary hive spawning boid particles that follow separation/alignment/cohesion rules plus player-seeking. Emergent collective behavior from simple local rules. Destroy the hive to disperse the swarm.
swarm_hive.name: Swarm Hive
swarm_hive.qfep_connection: Separation, alignment, cohesion — plus a fourth rule the textbooks omit: seek the player. Emergence weaponized, with one honest admission built in — even distributed behavior gets spawned from somewhere, and the hive is where you end it.

techstrider.description: Tall mechanical strider with long articulated legs. Patrols elevated paths, steps over obstacles. A walking architecture — the legs ARE the structure.
techstrider.name: Tech Strider
techstrider.qfep_connection: The gait is pure ornament: hip and knee swing on a 120-degree phase-offset sine while the body translates by fiat, never once asking the ground. Walking architecture, yes — but the walk is a costume the movement wears.

tentacle_cube.description: A cube with procedural tentacles extending from its faces. Combines rigid geometry with fluid organic motion — the grid cell that grew limbs.
tentacle_cube.name: Tentacle Cube
tentacle_cube.qfep_connection: A grid cell in good standing until you close within four meters — then the cube confesses, unfolding the jointed tentacles it had folded into rigidity. Category here is not a kind but a state with hysteresis: deploy at 4 m, retract at 6.

tesseract_phaser.description: Wireframe hypercube with 16 vertices and 32 edges. 4D rotation phases parts in and out of hittability — vertex alpha based on W-depth. The fourth dimension as combat mechanic.
tesseract_phaser.name: Tesseract Phaser
tesseract_phaser.qfep_connection: Most of its body sits at W-depths you cannot reach; combat is the thin slice where its four dimensions intersect your three. What reads as phasing trickery is projection being honest — the creature was always whole, you were always partial.

three_leg_critter.description: Three-legged procedural walker. Tripod gait — the minimum legs for static stability. Always has a support triangle.
three_leg_critter.name: Three Leg Critter
three_leg_critter.qfep_connection: Three planted feet make the first polygon that does not negotiate with falling; a leg may lift only when its stretch passes a threshold, so stability is not a state but a budget spent one foot at a time.

two_leg_critter.description: Two-legged procedural walker. Bipedal gait emerges from alternating step cycles. The simplest creature that must solve balance.
two_leg_critter.name: Two Leg Critter
two_leg_critter.qfep_connection: With two contacts there is no support polygon, only a line — so the code plants, stretches, and catches, and every stride is a fall filed under 'step'. Balance is bookkeeping done fast enough to look like poise.

waterbomb_enemy.description: True rigid-foldable origami enemy using waterbomb tessellation. Faces remain rigid during folding; geometry is computed from kinematic constraints. Rolls collapsed, unfolds to flower shape when attacking.
waterbomb_enemy.name: Waterbomb Enemy
waterbomb_enemy.qfep_connection: The shell does not fake it: rigid waterbomb faces fold under real geometric constraint, so the rolling ball and the open flower are one crease pattern read at two dihedral angles. Proximity, not damage, turns the page — approach is what makes it bloom.

waterbomb_hopper.description: Bouncing waterbomb tessellation enemy. Origami-themed hazard with a waterbomb base shape built from triangular faces. Bounces sinusoidally with squash-and-stretch, fold angle oscillates for a breathing effect. Patrols a rectangular path, chases on detection.
waterbomb_hopper.name: Waterbomb Hopper
waterbomb_hopper.qfep_connection: Its sibling blooms in place; this one reads the same fold as a spring — compression stores the hop, squash-and-stretch replays the crease as rhythm while it patrols its rectangle. One tessellation, two ontologies: origami as structure there, as stored energy here.

wave_rider.description: Ribbon of 20 box segments in sine wave formation. Oscillation frequency ramps on detection; attacks at resonance with projectile bursts. Wave physics as creature locomotion.
wave_rider.name: Wave Rider
wave_rider.qfep_connection: Twenty segments sampling one sine — no segment is the creature, the phase relation is. Being detected ramps its frequency toward resonance, and at the peak the wave discharges: attention literally raises its energy state.

catalyst_foe.name: Catalyst Foe
catalyst_foe.description: Biome-borne grey-goo foe. Walks toward the player one cell every step_period_s. When the catalyst projectile hits it (any mode — uses hit_by_projectile contract), phase-shifts to FRIEND state, takes the projectile color, and walks toward the nearest remaining foe to convert it on contact. The unifying enemy of Ada Research: the angry are biome-borne, the catalyst doesn't kill, transformation propagates.

catalyst_vent.name: Catalyst Vent
catalyst_vent.description: Biome corruption seam that emits CatalystFoe bodies on a timer until wave_size is reached, then goes quiet. Tall translucent grey pillar so the spawn point is visible from any camera angle. VR mirror of the /editor e:RATE:WAVE utility token.

death_pylon.description: A pylon stand that breathes death in a cycle. During the charge it drinks energy from the ground - a wide field of grid-cells and energy motes is sucked up into its swelling, brightening core (a GPUParticlesAttractorSphere3D pulling everything inward through the glowing intake ring). At full charge it fires a jet of fire straight at the player and, within kill_range, kills them via the DeathEffect autoload. Then it dims, gathers again, and repeats. The lesson is conservation: it takes from the world a long time before it gives it all back at once. Particle technique adapted from the godot-xr-tools particle galleries (additive fire gradient, attractor suck).
death_pylon.name: Death Pylon

parameters.charge_time: seconds to fully charge before firing (default 4.2)
parameters.cooldown_time: seconds to recover before charging again (default 1.5)
parameters.kill_range: radius within which the discharge kills the player (default 9.0)
parameters.grid_n: NxN ground grid that gets sucked in (default 5)
parameters.preview: 0..1 - jump into the charge for a still capture
parameters.preview_fire: bool - force the discharge for a capture

edge_zone_crystal.name: Edge Zone — Crystal (order-death)
edge_zone_crystal.description: A zone frozen at pure order (lambda=0): a cold crystalline lattice that harms while it holds its dead-perfect shape. Stand in it to RETUNE it toward the living edge (lambda~0.4) — it goes green and quiet; walk away and it freezes again. The thesis-mechanic: the world tries to freeze, you keep it alive.
edge_zone_crystal.qfep_connection: Lambda decays toward zero — the F_order death, the completed lattice — unless a body stands in the ring and retunes it back to 0.4. Order left alone finishes itself, and finishing is fatal: damage ticks precisely when the zone is most resolved.

edge_zone_dissolve.name: Edge Zone — Dissolve (chaos-death)
edge_zone_dissolve.description: A zone boiling at pure chaos (lambda=1): formless magenta particles scattering, harming while nothing can hold. Stand in it to RETUNE it toward the living edge (lambda~0.4); leave and it dissolves again. The other of the two deaths — both fail the same way, and life is the edge held between them.
edge_zone_dissolve.qfep_connection: The mirror death: lambda drifts to one, pure E_flux, the zone boiling into particles that keep no form. The same living 0.4 must be held from the opposite side — proof that the edge is not a compromise between order and chaos but a position approached against either drift.
